findings.description: The Park Emergency Hospital at 811 Stanyan Street, on the park's Kezar Corner, was built by park employees for $8,488 to designs by the city architect Newton J. Tharp — one of the few Beaux-Arts hospital buildings left, with sandstone walls and a red tile roof — and dedicated on May 15. The next morning its newly hired ambulance driver, James Wynn, was run over by his own bolting team as he unloaded supplies, the first member of the city's emergency hospital service to die on duty.
